Definition: from G1909 and a derivative of G4639; to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence:--overshadow.
BiblicalUsage: Episkiazo means to overshadow, to cast a shade upon. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; a bright cloud overshadowed them on the mountain, and a voice said, This is my beloved Son; and the sick were laid in the streets, that the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.
TheologicalSignificance: A cloud on the mountain, the Spirit on Mary, a shadow on the street — and in each case, power follows the shade. I hold that the overshadowing is God's nearness made visible, and I should expect His presence to bring His power with it.
RelatedTopics: Presence of God; Outpouring of the Spirit; Jesus Christ
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Simon Peter; Mary, Mother of Jesus
